::: {.callout-note}
## Known to exist — copy sought
An independent 1987 evaluation of Creekview 202 is attested in public secondary sources inspected for this catalogue. This archive has **not** recovered the evaluation itself. The creator attribution “Patricia Ryan / Ryan & Wiggins” still comes only from [jordanforge-infrastructure issue 10](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/jordanforge-infrastructure/issues/10); public searches in 2026 did not independently confirm that name on a title page or catalogue record.
:::

| Evaluation date as later stated | “In 1987 an independent evaluation of Creekview 202 was published” ([Haw 1989](haw-1989-creekview-account.qmd)) |

: Identification

## Annotation

This record remains a **wanted primary source**. What has been inspected is later public writing *about* an evaluation, not the evaluation.

Norman Haw, speaking as Director of Rehabilitation Services for the Canadian Paraplegic Association at the November 1989 Pacific Northwest Regional Polio Conference, said Creekview 202 opened in September 1985 and that a 1987 independent evaluation reported three findings: tenant-care cost about 60% of Pearson Hospital; government per-diem savings of about $100 a day (about $215,000 a year combined); health status at least as good as at Pearson, with physical health maintained and mental health and social interaction improved; and Canadian Council of Hospital Accreditation standards met or exceeded. Haw did not name the evaluator or give a formal title-page citation.

[SCI BC’s history page](sci-bc-history.qmd) places “Creekview” in 1985 as “the world’s first integrated, self-managed housing project with shared support services for people with high-level quadriplegia.” [Pamela Fayerman (2018)](fayerman-2018-walt-lawrence.qmd) attributes to Walt Lawrence a statement that CPA helped with an early-1980s cost analysis and that a study found community living about 30 percent less expensive than the rehabilitation facility. That percentage does not match Haw’s “approximately 60%” of Pearson costs. The two later accounts are catalogued; they are not treated as the same document.

Searches of WorldCat (title and Ryan/Wiggins queries), Internet Archive, UBC Library HTML search, and the open web did not recover a title-page PDF, ISBN, or library holding for “Creekview 202 Project Evaluation Report.”

## Open questions

- Exact title-page wording, pagination, place of publication, and report number.
- Whether Patricia Ryan / Ryan & Wiggins is the 1987 evaluator named by later writers.
- Where a copy now lives (CPA/SCI BC files, ministry records, personal papers, Legislative Library).
- Whether Haw’s 1987 evaluation, Fayerman’s “cost analysis,” and the commissioning-issue report are one document or several.
- What “202” refers to on the original title page (unit number is later used for the Creekview Co-op suite).
